title: Atomicity for payload contracts and deferred-invoke tool behavior acceptance
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: consumers of streamed structured responses and function/tool calls see inconsistent partial payloads when errors, retries, or backpressure occur. PRD goal: define a clear acceptance surface that balances portability (simple JSON schema), operational simplicity (deterministic retry and idempotency semantics), and user-facing guarantees (either atomic logical payloads or well-documented partial emission semantics). This ticket defines the acceptance criteria, error-mode matrix, observability hooks, and fallback patterns for deferred-invoke (tool-call) scenarios and mixed streaming + schema payloads. It also scopes non-goals (full transactional semantics across external tool side-effects).
acceptance_criteria: Schema contract: For every tool invocation emitted by the model, a root 'call' object MUST appear in the stream in a single discrete chunk when the model is able to emit it atomically (fast path). The 'call' object schema: { 'id': string, 'tool': string, 'args': object, 'intent': string, 'attempt': int }. For streaming partials the model SHOULD instead emit a 'call_fragment' series with a terminal 'call_complete' event that reconstructs the full call. (See test vectors)

Partial emission semantics: When a 'call_fragment' sequence occurs, the platform MUST deliver fragments in-order to the customer SDK and provide reconstruction helpers server-side. Consumers must be able to treat reconstructed call as equivalent to atomic 'call' for downstream tool routing and idempotency checks.

Idempotency and attempt counter: Every emitted call must include an 'id' (UUID v4) and an 'attempt' counter. The routing gateway MUST use (id, attempt) to deduplicate or detect retried invocations. Retry logic for transient errors MUST increment 'attempt' and preserve 'id'.

Failure modes & fallbacks: Define three error classes: transient (network/GPU OOM), soft schema deviation (missing fields/invalid types), and hard semantic error (forbidden tool or security violation). Each class has required platform reactions: transient => automatic retry up to N=2 and convert streaming in-flight to 'retry_marker' + new 'call' with same id and attempt increment; soft schema deviation => emit 'schema_warning' telemetry and attach 'repair_hint' where possible, do NOT invoke tool automatically; hard semantic error => emit 'tool_rejected' event and do not attempt automatic invoke.

Streaming checkpoints: For streamed responses containing both human-visible text tokens and structured call emissions, the runtime MUST produce periodic checkpoints (every 512 tokens or on 'call' boundaries) that include KV-cache-safe offsets and a monotonic sequence number to enable resumed reads and partial replay during client reconnects.

Observability: Each call lifecycle (emit -> reconstruct -> invoke -> completion/rollback) MUST produce traceable spans with the call.id attached. Console should show per-call latency, attempts, bytes emitted, and schema_validation_pass/fail boolean. Telemetry payloads must be accessible via the existing tracing/console APIs.

Backpressure & graceful degrade: When server-side batching or allocation forces truncation of a call emission, runtime MUST surface a 'call_aborted_truncated' event with reason and a canonical 'resume_hint' payload that SDKs can present to end users or product logic. The system MAY route to a compatible lighter-weight model variant automatically if 'resume_hint' indicates sequence continuation is possible.

Security gating: If tool invocation would access a restricted surface (per RBAC/KMS policy), the platform must emit 'tool_blocked' with an audit_reason and link to the audit log entry. Blocked calls are recorded as 'rejected' and must surface as explicit failures to caller code paths rather than silent no-ops.

E2E tests: Provide automated tests covering atomic call, fragmented call reconstruction, idempotent retry (same id, incremented attempt), transient failure retry, soft-schema-detection and repair_hint, hard rejection, and resume-after-disconnect using recorded replay harnesses. Tests must run in CI against the runtime-1.22 canary and the console-2026.03 dashboard builder.

User-facing SDK contract: SDKs must expose a 'callLifecycle' API with events: onFragment, onCallEmitted, onCallReconstructed, onInvokeStart, onInvokeComplete, onInvokeError. The API signatures must be stable for GA and documented in the SDK changelog entry before the release.

Metrics & SLO: New per-call metrics: calls_emitted_total, calls_reconstructed_total, calls_retries_total, calls_rejected_total, average_call_latency_ms. These must be emitted to our metrics pipeline and dashboards created prior to GA. GA requires <1% of calls ending in unrecoverable partial state for synthetic workload.

Migration & backward compatibility: For customers on legacy streaming contracts (pre-2026), the runtime MUST support a compatibility mode that wraps older 'function_call' tokens into the new 'call' envelope with generated ids but logs a migration_warning tag; this mode must be opt-in for the first release and documented in the migration guide.
notes: Design decisions / trade-offs: we chose not to attempt distributed two-phase commit for tool side-effects (out of scope) and instead emphasize idempotency and strong audit logs. Trade-off: fragmented emit reconstruction adds complexity to runtime and SDK; mitigated by server-side reconstruction helpers and CI test harness. Ops decision: default retry N=2; we can make it configurable per customer tier in Dedicated. See open question about exposing 'repair_hint' format to customers (current suggestion: short JSON pointer + human message).
